title: Recipe Repeat vs Novelty Mix
dataSources: Mealime meal plans (`mealime:plan`), AnyList grocery lists (`anylist:grocery`), Instacart orders (`instacart:order`), Paprika recipes (`paprika:recipe`), and pantry inventory counts (`pantry:inventory`).
app: Mealime weekly plans, AnyList grocery lists, Instacart order history, Paprika recipe exports, and pantry inventory scans ingested into Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=paprika:recipe recipe_name=* cook_count=*
| eval cooked_recently=if(relative_time(_time,"@w0"),1,0)
| stats sum(cooked_recently) as cooks_this_week, dc(recipe_name) as unique_recipes
| eval repeat_ratio=round(100*cooks_this_week/unique_recipes,1)
description: Measures how often Paprika recipes cooked this week are repeats versus new additions.
value: Too much repetition breeds meal fatigue; too much novelty wastes ingredients already in the pantry.
implementation: Track `cook_count` and recipe name on each Paprika cook event and review the repeat ratio monthly.
visualization: Donut chart of repeat versus new recipe cooks.
grandmaExplanation: It counts whether you are mostly reheating the same recipes or actually trying new ones.
